Summary (auto): Follow-up on Friday reliability incident that produced intermittent 5xxs/timeouts for a subset of traffic. Focus on reproducing, extracting request_ids, and confirming retry behavior.

Transcript:
[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — run through what we saw friday night, what we've hypothesized, and actions to reproduce and remediate. carlos, do you want to start with what you observed?
[00:18] Carlos: yeah, sure. so we had a spike in 5xxs around 22:14 UTC, basically a mix of 503 and some upstream timeouts. about, uh, 3-4% of requests in that 20 minute window. most were coming from one customer-facing route.
[00:36] Aisha: and to add, our client shows repeated retries — we saw exponential backoff but some of the retries also hit rate limits shortly after which cascaded.
[00:50] Tom: i'm seeing in the ingress that there were a couple of connection resets, and our nginx logs show a brief RTT spike. i pulled the GCLB logs and uploaded them to the shared folder: [link: gclb-logs-mar31.log].
[01:05] Sasha: ok, thanks. from Redwood side we see a burst of concurrent long-lived requests which increased memory pressure on a few hosts, and our autoscaler didn't kick in fast enough due to the configured cooldown. that's one hypothesis. also possible we hit a rate limit on the model backend and saw 5xx upward.
[01:24] Carlos: when you say "model backend" you mean your hosted infra? we are on the dedicated pilot but traffic is routed through Redwood infer control plane right?
[01:36] Morgan: yeah, to clarify — you're on Redwood Dedicated but the control plane still mediates routing and can trigger fallbacks/limits. sometimes errors get bubbled as 5xx from the runtime. apologies, people sometimes call it Redwood Infer, that's our internal shorthand.
[01:53] Tom: there's also the KV cash — sorry cache — we noticed some cache misses which might have forced more work per request. Aisha's batch sizes were higher than usual so more token compute.
[02:09] Aisha: yup, we increased max tokens in the prompt for edge cases; that plus a bad arrival pattern could be the trigger.
[02:20] Morgan: okay, so hypotheses: 1) transient host pressure + slow autoscale, 2) rate-limit/routing thresholds hit causing 5xx, 3) specific request patterns triggering longer KV cache warmups. we should try to reproduce.
[02:35] Sasha: action — SE will run a 1.5x load test against staging with the same arrival distribution and max_token settings, and we'll capture full request traces with request_ids. please make sure to send those request_ids for the Friday window too.
[02:48] Carlos: we'll get the ids. quick Q: you mentioned cooldowns — can you tune autoscaler so it reacts faster?
[02:57] Sasha: there's a balance — lowering cooldown reduces tail latencies because you get faster scale up, but you can overscale and increase cost. we can propose a more aggressive policy for the pilot window. also enabling burst capacity can help.
[03:14] Tom: and on retries — our code currently retries on 5xx with fixed delay; if we implement jittered exponential backoff client-side would that reduce the thundering herd?
[03:25] Sasha: yes, jittered exponential backoff helps. also consider respecting the x-retry-after header from the platform if we return 429-like signals. right now some 5xxs didn't have explicit retry headers, which complicates client logic.
[03:40] Aisha: are there logs or a dashboard I can look at for token-level breakdown? our model usage profile would help tune batch sizes.
[03:48] Morgan: check the Redwood Console dashboard — i shared a link in the deck earlier [link: pilot-dashboard]. i'll resend it after the call. token/latency breakdowns per route are available.
[03:59] Carlos: about security/compliance — procurement wants the SOC2 packet before approving an extension. can you resend SOC2 and ISO docs? and also KMS details for dedicated?
[04:12] Morgan: yes, i'll attach SOC2, ISO, and our KMS/HSM notes to the pilot extension email.
[04:20] Tom: any chance the 5xxs were synthetic from a third-party dependency? we have a downstream enrichment service that flattens the payload and that had an incident too.
[04:30] Aisha: good point, we've seen correlation but not causation. that's why we need the raw request_ids and the full traces.
[04:38] Sasha: technical note — when you send traces, include the runtime request_id from the x-rw-request-id header. that maps to our logs. if you only have client ids it's ok, but runtime ids are ideal.
[04:50] Carlos: we'll pull runtime ids from Friday's window and share.
[04:54] Morgan: ok next steps then — SE runs load test, customer provides ids, AE sends extension + security docs. if the load test reproduces the 5xxs we'll schedule an infra deep-dive next week with ops on both sides.
[05:07] Tom: one more thing — can you share suggested client retry code? we have a Java microservice doing retries.
[05:14] Sasha: yes, i have a snippet i'll post to the repo: exponential backoff with jitter, honoring Retry-After. also suggest circuit-breaker at the route level to avoid cascading.
[05:27] Aisha: and about the KV cache behavior — is there a way to pre-warm the KV to avoid cache-storms on rollout?
[05:35] Sasha: we can pre-warm prefix entries for the pilot, yep. also recommend pinning model version for the test so we don't mix variants.
[05:45] Carlos: sounds good. timeline expectation? we need results before next Tuesday to make extension decision mid-week.
[05:53] Morgan: we'll aim for SE results by Friday (2026-04-02) and AE pricing by Monday (2026-04-05). that should give you time to review.
[06:02] Tom: ack. thanks everyone.
[06:04] Morgan: thanks, we'll follow up in the thread with links. bye.
